A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same B-STAR study and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G. Relocated material can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original training and evaluation results on mathematical reasoning, coding, and commonsense reasoning, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, and appendix configuration studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1–6 and the training-dynamics and configuration analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The balance score, iterative temperature and reward-threshold optimization, response selection, and policy updates remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 moves from the main text to the appendix pages without changing its procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain MATH training, MATH500 and GSM8K evaluation, APPS coding experiments, and ARC-Challenge commonsense reasoning. No dataset, task, or distinct test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain SFT, STaR/ReST-EM, Iterative RFT, and Online RFT, including the same reward-model variants and fixed-configuration controls. The new Appendix B.1 heading contains previously documented baseline descriptions.

E3.justification: The data partitions, model choices, training budgets, candidate counts, search grids, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. Settings removed from the shortened Section 4.1 remain documented in Appendices A–B.

E4.justification: Both retain the exploration/exploitation case study, temperature-versus-threshold ablation in Table 3, sample-size analysis in Figure 4(c), finer-grained configuration study in Appendix D, and fixed-configuration comparisons in Appendix E.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The statistical reporting practices and absence of error bars remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 and the plotted results match across versions. For example, Table 1 retains B-STAR Pass@1 scores of 53.8 on GSM8K, 27.8 on MATH, 19.6 on APPS, and 73.0 on ARC-C. Appendix results are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The Pass@K-S and Reward@K-S definitions, balance-score equation, reward and RFT formulations in Appendix C, and reinforcement-learning derivation in Appendix G are retained. No mathematical correction or new proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged, and both versions retain the core claims about monitoring exploration/exploitation, balancing them through B-STAR, and improving self-training across the evaluated reasoning and coding tasks. Shortened introduction and discussion wording does not redefine the contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 removes the additional inference that Figure 1 further validates B-STAR's generalizability. This locally trims the interpretation; the mechanism explanations, reward-model caveats, and stronger-model generalization discussion in Section 4.3 remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, PRM training details, data-processing information, and the code-access statement remain available. Relocating Algorithm 1 and consolidating setup descriptions in Appendix B neither adds technical information nor removes reproducibility details.

R1.justification: The bibliography and Appendix F's research positioning are unchanged. A repeated Singh et al. citation is omitted from footnote 2, but that work remains cited and discussed elsewhere; no cited work or substantive relationship to prior research is added or removed.

P1.justification: v2 condenses Section 4.1, moves baseline explanations into a separately headed Appendix B.1, and renumbers the following setup subsections. Scattered wording is shortened, and the Preprint header becomes an ICLR 2025 publication header. The overall narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: Algorithm 1 moves from v1 page 8 to v2 page 15. Several figures and tables are repositioned, and some displays are slightly resized, including Figures 5–6. All eight figures and six tables retain their content and basic design.

improvement.justification: v2 primarily reorganizes the same method, evidence, mathematical content, and reproducibility information. The shorter setup and small interpretive trim provide limited editorial benefits, while moving Algorithm 1 to the appendix makes it less immediately accessible. These modest changes leave the paper's overall quality essentially unchanged.
